headline: Ecuador's Wasteful Dominance
story: Ecuador dominated entirely—66 per cent possession, 27 shots, the high press applied at 4.1 phases. Curaçao sat in a 5-4-1, invited nothing, forced only 0.8 pressing situations. The blueprint was established in the opening minute: Ecuador would pin them deep; Curaçao would defend with discipline. Both teams understood the script. The question was only whether Ecuador could finish.

They couldn't. Their expected goals totalled 2.76 against Curaçao's meagre 0.63, yet the scoresheet read 0-0 when the final whistle came. Eloy Room, rated 10.0, was immaculate—he saved efforts with xG of 0.49 in the third minute, 0.32 in the twentieth, and 0.24 in the fifty-ninth, before a high-quality chance (0.37) was blocked in the sixty-sixth. Ecuador's ball-recovery advantage of 8.2 seconds to Curaçao's 20.4 gave them tempo; it gifted them nothing.

keyMoment.text: Room's save (0.24 xG) in the fifty-ninth; Ecuador's winning moment never arrives.

home.verdict: Dominance without a finish is a non-result.
points: Four big chances (0.49, 0.32, 0.24, 0.37 xG) missed: clinical composure decided it.
27 shots, 15 on target, 2.76 xG: quality of finish, not volume, was the gap.
Ball-recovery edge (8.2s vs 20.4s) created space; conversion rate, not creation, failed.

away.verdict: Room's perfection masked the gamble's fragility.
points: Eloy Room's 10.0 rating: one lapse, one goal conceded, and this becomes a defeat.
Ball-recovery time (20.4s) killed counter-potential; faster transitions were non-negotiable.
Defensive discipline (5-4-1 formation) held; one clinical Ecuador finish ends it all.

statLine: Ecuador squandered 2.76 expected goals from 27 shots; Eloy Room's 10.0 rating summoned something immeasurable.
